name: The Data Trusts Initiative
tagline: Working at the interface of technology, policy and the law to create data trusts that empower individuals and communities while supporting data use for social benefit.
news_articles: Data trusts could help patients control their health records (The Guardian, 2021)
How data trusts could give people control over their personal information (Wired, 2021)
academic_citations: Delacroix & Lawrence (2019) — Bottom-up data trusts, Internet Policy Review
Montgomery et al. (2021) — Data Governance for the 21st Century
Global Partnership on AI (2022) — Enabling Data Sharing for Social Benefit Through Data Trusts

policy_outcomes.description: Submission to UK AI Council's Exploring Legal Mechanisms for Data Stewardship
Three real-world data trust pilots launched: Born in Scotland Data Trust, Brixham Data Trust, GP Data Trust

documented_limitations: Legal frameworks for data trusts remain underspecified in UK law
failure_modes: Unresolved legal status of data trusts
curation_criteria: Academic research-driven; focus on legal and policy frameworks for data trusts; community benefit orientation
contributor_governance: Academic institution governance (University of Cambridge); advisory board structure
community_ownership: Limited; primarily researcher-led with community input through pilot projects
legal_regulatory_issues: Ongoing uncertainty regarding legal status and enforceability of data trusts under UK law; GDPR compliance considerations
ai_involvement: Limited; focus is on data governance and legal frameworks rather than AI systems, though AI governance is contextually relevant
